table.title: Document ingestion environment variables
table.html:
NameRequiredDefaultDescription
DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAMEYesNoneName of the S3-compatible bucket where uploaded source files and derived page images are stored; the bucket must already exist and be in the same region as the worker fleet.
DATABASE_CONNECTION_POOL_MAX_SIZENo20Maximum number of PostgreSQL connections each API pod may hold; increase only after confirming the PgBouncer pool has sufficient headroom.
OCR_PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDSNo300Wall-clock limit for a single OCR job before the worker marks the attempt as failed and schedules a retry with exponential backoff.
JWT_SIGNING_KEY_ROTATION_INTERVAL_HOURSNo168Interval between automatic signing-key rotations; retired keys remain accepted for token verification for twice this duration.
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINSNohttps://app.example.comComma-separated list of exact origins permitted to call browser-facing endpoints; wildcard entries are rejected when the service runs in production mode.
FEATURE_FLAG_ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_INDEXINGNofalseEnables delta indexing after document updates; when disabled, a full reindex is required before changes appear in search results.
SMTP_RELAY_HOSTNAMEConditionallocalhostHostname of the outbound mail relay used for invitations and alerts; required when EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE is set to smtp and ignored when it is set to ses.
table.brief: Environment variables: Name (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE long names) / Required / Default / Description

understanding.purpose: Document the environment variables used to configure document ingestion and explain when and how to set them.
understanding.reading: Readers scan variable names to find a setting, then compare whether it is required, its default, and its description. Each row must remain easy to follow across the table; on a phone, horizontal scrolling can preserve readable values at the cost of hiding later columns initially.
groups: Name identifies each row and anchors the other values.
Required and Default are compact configuration facts that readers compare across rows.
Description explains the setting and may need substantially more space than the compact fact columns.
keep_intact: Environment variable names, because they are exact identifiers readers may copy.
Default values and other code-like tokens where possible.
Required values, including longer qualifiers, where practical.
may_wrap: Description prose can wrap at word boundaries; longer descriptions can use the height already created by wrapping elsewhere in the same row.
Headers and multiword status text can wrap naturally.

preferred.name: r2C
preferred.note: Retain r1B's initial view of Name and Required, but widen Description to reduce the tall rows. This tests whether the visibility of status justifies splitting several identifiers.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Preserve exact identifiers and values, and give descriptions a full phone-width column to improve prose rhythm and reduce row height, accepting more horizontal scrolling.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Keep identifiers and compact values intact while reducing Description from r1C's 360px to 300px. This tests whether a moderate prose width can retain much of its better row rhythm with less horizontal scrolling.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Fit the Name column within the initial viewport and reserve generous space for prose. A few of the longest identifiers may split, but most names should be visible in full before scrolling.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Keep all names intact as in r2A, but use r2B's wider description column to reduce row height. This favors exact identifiers and accepts a wide horizontal scroll.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Retain r2C's useful initial view of Name and Required, while narrowing Description to reduce horizontal travel. Check whether the resulting extra prose wrapping is an acceptable cost.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Fit Name and Required within 359px so both are visible initially; accept wrapped identifiers while preserving defaults and giving descriptions a usable width.
bad.why: The narrow description column makes the table substantially taller and leaves large empty areas in the visible name and required columns.

bad.name: r3C
bad.note: Give names more room than r2C while keeping the table narrower than r2B. Test whether fewer identifier breaks justify showing only part of Required initially.
bad.why: The name column breaks several identifiers awkwardly, including an isolated final letter, while pushing part of the required column outside the initial viewport.

rationale: r2C brings both the row names and the complete Required column into the initial viewport, letting readers identify variables and scan their status together. Its wider description column keeps rows reasonably compact, although readers must scroll to see defaults and descriptions. Several names wrap within identifier components, a real cost of fitting the status column on screen.

general: Prioritize columns that readers need to compare together in the initial viewport.
Judge horizontal scrolling and row height together; a narrower table can create excessive vertical whitespace.
Keep identifiers intact where practical, and inspect actual wrap points when space is constrained.
specific: A 260px Name column and 99px Required column fit together within the 360px viewport.
The 320px Description column in r2C reduces row height substantially compared with the 220px column in r1B.

tradeoffs: r1C and r3A preserve full identifiers within their columns, but the initial viewport shows essentially only names and requires more horizontal scrolling. r3B reduces scrolling compared with r2C, at the cost of taller rows.
uncertain: A designer may prioritize intact variable names over seeing Required immediately, particularly for readers who copy identifiers. The ranges are approximate design judgments; exact wrap points and equivalent quality within them have not been verified by additional renders.

critique.good: Identifiers, status values and defaults remain intact, and the description has enough width for relatively comfortable prose. Rows are distinct and all headers stay on one line.
critique.problems: The initial viewport shows almost exclusively the Name column, with the ends of the longest names beyond the viewport. Readers must scroll a long way to reach the configuration facts and descriptions; the tall rows also leave large blank areas under short names.
critique.cause: The 398px Name column alone exceeds the viewport, and the 190px Default and 300px Description columns extend the total width to 988px.

critique.good: The initial viewport exposes the Name and most of Required, giving readers an earlier view of a useful configuration fact. It substantially reduces horizontal scrolling while retaining single-line headers and a reasonably wide description.
critique.problems: Several exact variable names break across lines at arbitrary points, making them harder to scan and copy. The longest Required value extends beyond the initial viewport, and at least one long token elsewhere splits. Blank space remains in shorter cells because descriptions determine row height.
critique.cause: The 280px Name column provides only 259px for identifiers, the 99px Required column extends past the viewport when placed after it, and the 130px Default column cannot contain the longest default intact.

critique.good: All four columns are visible at once, and their order makes the relationship between each setting and its facts immediately apparent.
critique.problems: Identifiers, headers, status text, defaults and description words break in the middle. Descriptions form very narrow vertical strips, making rows exceptionally tall and comparison difficult.
critique.cause: All four columns must share 359px: after padding, the 125px Name, 65px Required, 70px Default and 99px Description columns provide too little text width for their contents.

critique.good: The full-width Name column keeps identifiers intact, and the Required and Default columns have enough room for their longest values. Row boundaries provide a consistent structure for following each setting across the table.
critique.problems: The initial viewport shows only the Name column, with long identifiers extending beyond its right edge. The rows are very tall, leaving large areas of empty space under most names and making the list harder to scan.
critique.cause: Name is 398px wide, already wider than the viewport. The 240px Description column wraps prose into as many as seven lines, setting the height of rows whose other cells contain much less text.

critique.good: Name and Required are visible together at first, so readers can scan identifiers alongside their status. The overall table is narrower than r1A, reducing horizontal travel.
critique.problems: Several identifiers visibly break across lines, sometimes inside a word, making exact names harder to read and copy. Tall rows still leave substantial empty space, and Default and Description require scrolling.
critique.cause: The 260px Name column provides only 239px of text space, which is too narrow for several identifiers. The 220px Description column produces extensive wrapping and dominates row height.

critique.good: Identifiers and compact values have room to remain intact. The wider Description column gives prose a more comfortable measure and produces a much tighter vertical rhythm than r1A, with fewer large blank areas.
critique.problems: The initial view contains only names, and the longest names extend past the viewport. Readers must scroll a long way to reach Description, despite its contribution to the improved row rhythm.
critique.cause: The 398px Name column exceeds the viewport, while the 360px Description column brings the total width to 1048px.

critique.good: The full-width name column keeps identifiers intact, and the compact fact columns have enough room for their values.
critique.problems: The initial viewport shows only the name column and cuts off the ends of the longest names. Large blank areas beneath short names weaken the row rhythm, while the remaining information requires substantial sideways scrolling.
critique.cause: At 398px, Name is wider than the viewport; the 300px Description column also creates tall rows and adds considerably to the total width.

critique.good: The wider description column reduces row heights, and most names remain on one line. Required and Default retain room for their values.
critique.problems: Two long identifiers break within words, and the initial viewport still shows almost none of Required. Tall rows leave conspicuous blank space under shorter names.
critique.cause: The 350px Name column is too narrow for the longest identifiers but nearly fills the viewport. The 320px Description column contributes to a 960px table.

critique.good: Name and Required are visible together initially, making the first scan more useful. The table is narrower than the other two designs, and the fact columns retain readable values.
critique.problems: Most long identifiers wrap, sometimes in the middle of a word, making exact names harder to scan and copy. Default and Description still require sideways scrolling.
critique.cause: The 260px Name column leaves only 239px for identifier text. The 99px Required column fits beside it, but the combined widths leave no meaningful space for Default in the initial viewport.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r2A.why: Names stay mostly on one line, but the initial viewport shows only the name column and cuts off the longest identifiers. Tall rows leave substantial blank space.

ref_equal.why: All four columns fit in the viewport, but identifiers and description words break into fragments, making the rows extremely tall and difficult to scan.

ref_auto.why: Only the name column is visible initially, some names extend beyond the viewport, and the very tall rows make it hard to compare entries.

r1B.why: Names and required status appear together in the viewport, though several identifiers split awkwardly. Tall rows and the need to scroll for defaults and descriptions slow comparison.

r1C.why: Compact rows and mostly intact names make the first column easy to scan, but the viewport shows no other column and cuts off the longest names.

r2C.why: Names and required status are visible together, with a more compact row rhythm than D. Several identifiers split midword, and defaults and descriptions require horizontal scrolling.

raw.unsure: The supplied views of A and C–F do not show the full table width, so I cannot assess the off-screen columns or the full scrolling distance directly.

r1C.why: Names appear intact, but the initial viewport shows only the name column, and the longest names extend beyond it. The other columns are not visible in the supplied image.

r2C.why: Name and Required fit together in the viewport, making the first scan useful. Several identifiers split within words, and the remaining columns are outside the supplied image.

ref_equal.why: All four columns fit, but identifiers, ordinary words, the URL, and even the Description header fragment into very narrow columns. The resulting tall rows are difficult to read across.

ref_auto.why: The viewport shows only names, with substantial empty space in each row and the longest names extending beyond the viewport. The other columns are not visible in the supplied image.

r1B.why: Name and Required fit together, but identifiers split within words and the rows have considerable empty space in the visible columns. The remaining columns are outside the supplied image.

r2A.why: Names appear intact, but the viewport shows only the name column and the longest names extend beyond it. The other columns are not visible in the supplied image.

raw.unsure: The supplied images for A, B, D, E, and F end near the viewport edge, so I cannot assess the full widths or readability of their Default and Description columns, or the full cost of horizontal scrolling. B is the strongest of the visible portions.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
